About B2Spin

We are B2Spin, and we are dedicated to delivering the best Free-to-Play Social Casino and gaming experiences by creating captivating, engaging, and unique products that are accessible to everyone. We have built a team of talented professionals from all over the globe, who are working to continually improve the experiences of our players. We are not looking to just be part of the industry, but to revolutionize it.

The role

B2Spin is looking for a Payments & Fraud Data Analyst to join our Business Intelligence team and help keep money moving safely through our platform. You'll turn transactional and player-behaviour data into clear insight that improves payment performance, prevents fraud and abuse, and protects the experience for genuine players — working closely with Payments, Fraud, Compliance and Operations to make their decisions sharper and faster.

What you'll do

 - Own payment performance analytics end to end — diving into success rates, declines, payment methods and provider performance to surface improvements that reduce friction and cost.

 - Uncover fraud and abuse patterns across transactional and behavioural data — from promo abuse and multi-accounting to chargebacks and money cycling — and translate findings into actionable rules, thresholds and segments.

 - Design, back-test and monitor automated risk decisions, balancing fraud capture against player friction and tracking real-world impact after every change goes live.

 - Build the reporting layer that keeps the business informed — dashboards in Looker or Tableau, plus alerts for business-critical anomalies like provider volume drops or risk spikes.

 - Partner with Compliance on AML work, delivering investigation queries, data analysis and audit-ready reporting that hold up to scrutiny.

 - Accelerate Operations and Customer Service with analytics that quantify review workloads, case outcomes and player-facing friction so teams move faster and more consistently.

 - Raise the analytical bar across the business — documenting data sources, metric definitions and automation logic so insight is trusted, reusable and easy to build on.

What we're looking for

 - Hands-on data analyst background in payments, fraud, risk or AML — ideally within gaming, iGaming, fintech or another high-volume digital environment.

 - Strong SQL skills on a cloud data warehouse (BigQuery preferred) paired with practical experience in Looker, Tableau or Power BI.

 - Demonstrated experience analysing fraud and abuse patterns in transactional and behavioural data, with a clear understanding of the trade-off between fraud capture and friction for genuine players.

 - The ability to run analytical projects from ambiguity to delivery — scoping unclear questions, building solutions, documenting them and monitoring their impact over time.

 - Confident, clear communication across Operations, Compliance and senior leadership, including the ability to challenge assumptions with data in a remote-team setting.

 - An investigative instinct and sharp attention to detail — you notice when something looks off and you follow it until you understand why.

 - Python for deeper analysis, anomaly detection or modelling is a strong plus, as is familiarity with fraud-scoring tools, device or behavioural signals, social casino mechanics, or ML approaches to fraud detection.

Our values

At B2Spin, passion means we genuinely love what we build — and we surround ourselves with people who feel the same way. Performance means we back that passion with accountability: we move fast, own our results, and choose progress over perfection every time.

Equal opportunities

We hire based on skills, drive, and ideas — nothing else. Your background, gender, age, race, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, religion, neurodiversity, or educational path will never be a barrier to joining us. We also welcome candidates from non-traditional career journeys and value diverse perspectives that challenge conventional thinking. Diversity fuels our innovation, collaboration, and growth, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can contribute their best work and thrive.

About the role
Jade is Chime’s AI financial partner, helping members better understand and manage their money. We’re looking for a software engineer who enjoys building reliable systems, solving practical problems, and learning new technologies.
You’ll work on the services, APIs, and integrations behind Jade, helping our members interact with AI as part of their Chime experience. Our backend primarily uses Python, and we welcome engineers with strong experience in other languages who are interested in learning it. You’ll build capabilities for our members and help improve the quality, reliability, and performance of our new AI-powered product.
We value strong engineering fundamentals, thoughtful problem-solving, and curiosity. Prior experience or specialization in AI or machine learning is preferred, but not required. You’ll have opportunities to develop that knowledge on the team.
In this role, you can expect to
Design, build, and test backend services and APIs that power Jade’s capabilities.
Build integrations that connect AI models with member data, tools, and Chime services.
Own scoped features from technical design through implementation and rollout, with feedback and support from your teammates.
Contribute to automated evaluations, testing, and experiments that help us understand model behavior, measure quality, and catch regressions.
Improve system reliability, performance, and observability, and help investigate production issues.
Partner with engineering, product, design, and data teammates to understand member needs and iterate on useful experiences.
To thrive in this role, you have
2+ years developing software in a production environment at scale
Proficiency in a backend programming language, such as Python, Go or Ruby, and the ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code.
Experience building backend services or applications, including working with APIs and databases.
Strong systems thinking, you can reason about how components fit together, how data moves through a system, and where failures might occur.
An understanding of distributed systems fundamentals, including service communication, reliability, and trade-offs around latency, consistency, and scale.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, with the ability to break work into manageable steps and explain technical choices.
A collaborative approach, clear communication, and a willingness to ask questions, incorporate feedback, and learn unfamiliar technologies.
Preferred Qualifications
The following are preferred, but not required:
Experience with Python and its backend development ecosystem.
Familiarity with large language models (LLMs), including using model APIs, prompts, or tools to build applications.
Exposure to AI evaluations (“evals”), such as using test cases, datasets, or experiments to measure response quality and identify regressions.
Familiarity with AI tools and frameworks such as LangSmith, LangChain, LangGraph, Amazon Bedrock, or comparable platforms. Experience with any particular tool is not expected.
Experience deploying and supporting a production application, including monitoring, troubleshooting, or working with cloud infrastructure.
Your exposure to AI can come from professional work, personal projects, or hands-on learning. We welcome strong engineers who are interested in growing into this space.
